messages:
amy: quick q — when RLS routes a request to a cheaper model variant, do we still log the full req/resp for billing/audit? worried about turnstile accounting + PII scrub ordering. cc @ben :thinking:
ben: we currently attach a route tag after the routing decision but before sampling. so logs show which model served, but sampling happens after routing in the pipeline. that means cheaper-model requests can still be sampled and end up in audit buckets unless we exclude them.
chandra: is that exclusion per-tenant or global? tenant quotas rely on consistent counts; if we exclude some variants we might undercount usage for quota enforcement.
eli: short answer: three options
- sample-before-route: preserves tenant accounting (counts every request), but we lose information about which variant would have served when sample=0 (harder to debug rollouts)
- route-before-sample (today): accurate view of what served, but audit stores can overrepresent cheaper variants if not filtered by route
- hybrid: sample-before-route for quota meters, route-before-sample for audit/logging with separate lightweight counters
amy: hybrid sounds promising. how would scrub/redact fit in? we must avoid cleartext PII reaching cheap audit buckets or S3.
ben: recommend: 1) increment lightweight counters (route-independent) in the ingress path, 2) compute routing decision, 3) perform sampling for full capture, 4) run redaction pipeline before any long-term storage. that keeps quotas accurate and ensures redaction always applies before persistence.
eli: implementation nit: we need an "ingress-meter" event that is extremely small (route id, tenant id, token count) so it's cheap and non-sensitive. counters -> billing/quotas. then a separate "audit-capture" path that contains full payload only if sampled.
chandra: edgecase: embeddings + PII. embeddings are non-reversible usually but still sensitive (user names, emails). ops asked if we can transform embeddings to hashed provenance only. proposal: for embeddings route, store only:
```
{
  "tenant": "t-123",
  "route": "embeddings.lowcost.v1",
  "embedding_hash": "sha256(...)",
  "meta": {"length": 768}
}
```
no raw vectors unless tenant explicitly opts in.
amy: console UX question — if someone flips the "capture full logs" toggle during a rollout, how do we avoid a flood of storage and a partial audit window? debounce? staged propagation?
ben: we should do a 5-min rollout window: toggles in console create a feature-flag change that hits edge proxies after a short TTL. also show an estimated retention/cost projection dialog before enabling.
eli: plus a gating rule: if your tenant has >X qps to the route, require owner confirmation (modal) to enable capture. that prevents accidental huge bills.
chandra: also add a soft-cap on the number of full-capture events per hour that will be throttled and emit a warning in console + slack.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary deploy v2-routing-metering applied to staging at 3234567020 :rocket:
amy: ok decision summary: hybrid meters + route-aware sampling + redact-before-store. console: debounce toggles (5m) + cost modal + per-tenant confirmation > threshold. can we get a short PR that wires ingress-meter + audit-capture flag? @ben @eli please pair on an RFC this week. :thumbsup:
ben: on it, will draft RFC and include schema for ingress-meter (tenant, req_ts, token_count, route_hint).
eli: i'll mock console flow and cost modal screens and add thresholds.
chandra: i'll write embedding retention rule for audit buckets (hash-only by default).
amy: thanks everyone — tagging this resolved for planning unless we hit a blocker. :white_check_mark:
